evidences.title: Nicky Henderson says lacklustre Sprinter Sacre will miss Cheltenham | Sprinter Sacre | The Guardian
evidences.content:
Sprinter Sacre, the outstanding winner of last season's Queen Mother Champion Chase at Cheltenham, will miss this year's Festival meeting as he is "not showing the same brilliance as he did last season", according to Nicky Henderson, his trainer.

Sprinter Sacre was unbeaten over fences until his first start of the current campaign, when he was pulled up midway through a race at Kempton Park on 27 December and was subsequently found to be suffering from an irregular heartbeat.

The problem corrected itself while Sprinter Sacre was under observation by Celia Marr, a leading equine cardiologist, at a specialist unit in Newmarket, and the eight-year-old has subsequently undergone regular exercise with a heart monitor and without incident.

Most bulletins from the Henderson yard on Sprinter Sacre's progress have been broadly positive, and on Sunday morning he was still an odds-on favourite to win the Champion Chase at Cheltenham. His odds started to drift on the Betfair betting exchange during the day, however, prior to an announcement just after 6pm that he will not run again this season.

Henderson told the Racing Post that the decision to rule out Sprinter Sacre until the autumn was taken after he had worked on Saturday with Triolo D'Alene, the winner of the Hennessy Gold Cup in November.

"Sprinter's work over 10 furlongs was all right," Henderson said, "and with any other horse you'd think it was fine, but Sprinter is not showing the same brilliance as last season; he is just 10% short of that. Thankfully his heart is fine and there is no problem there.

"Having discussed options with Caroline and Raymond Mould [Sprinter Sacre's owners], Nico de Boinville, who has ridden him every morning for three seasons, and Celia Marr, who has been monitoring his heart, it was agreed that we should pull stumps for the time being. Now we will concentrate on getting Sprinter back next season to the same form he showed last season."

The failure of his stable star to return to the scene of his 19-length success in last year's Champion Chase is a new setback in a disappointing campaign for Henderson, who won the trainers' championship last season for the first time since 1987.

Sprinter Sacre may now be absent from the track at least until the Tingle Creek Chase at Sandown Park in December, which has been his initial target for his first run in each of the past two years. The news that he is simply not showing his normal form at home will also fuel concern that Sprinter Sacre may never return to the dominance and brilliance which characterised his first two seasons over fences.

"I said the other week it was 50-50 [that he would run at Cheltenham] but quietly I thought it was above that," Henderson said. "I honestly thought we were going the right way.

"It's just not all there and I can't ask a horse of his standing, I can't sacrifice him, I think it is fairer to everybody. The horse told us what he wanted to tell us yesterday. It's not what he's made of."
